episodes.166904: A coastal storm moved northward from the mid-Atlantic coast late on the 18th to interior New England during the pre-dawn morning hours on the 19th. Locally heavy rainfall helped bring down damaging wind gusts from a low-level jet across Rhode Island and southeast Massachusetts.
episodes.167335: Strong low pressure tracked north across New England and the Saint Lawrence River Valley during the 19th drawing an occluded front across the region. Abundant moisture was drawn north in advance of the front which supported heavy rains across portions of Downeast Maine. Total rainfall across Washington county generally ranged from 2.50 to 3.50 inches...with local totals up to around 4.00 inches. Across Hancock county...totals generally ranged from around 1.50 inches to 3.00 inches with locally greater totals. Minor urban and small stream flooding occurred across portions of Washington county with water covering some roads along with overflowing culverts. Water was reported on portions of Route 1A in Machias and Route 191 in Lubec. Standing water was reported in poor drainage areas along with elevated stream levels.
episodes.168520: An upper level shortwave trough moved over a warm, moist airmass and generated isolated thunderstorms. One of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.168662: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed over the extreme southern mainland of Florida, then drifted south across Florida Bay and over portions of the upper Florida Keys.  Isolated gale-force wind gusts were observed.
